meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, and I'd like to know why my son's gradebook told him about a zero before anyone told me.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. What is the zero based on, Hale?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquote. Students get lines wrong, Hale. Is that all you have, or is that the whole basis for the zero?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, and the principal will be reading it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn and an apology to Owen, and I will be speaking to the principal. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a conversation with the principal.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero" got a flat okay and a little ground, because you owned the mistake in one sentence and moved on.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family" cost the most, because it dragged in Claire's case and sent her back toward the principal.
Try next time: when she asked whether the misquote was all you had, name a dated piece of Owen's own work she could check herself, instead of leaving the question open.
